recognize_zh: 舌背、舌側與舌腹可見白色網狀（reticular）條紋與斑塊，伴隨舌乳頭萎縮與紅斑，唇緣也發紅，是口腔 cGVHD 的苔蘚樣（lichenoid）表現，屬 NIH 口腔 cGVHD 的診斷性徵象。
features: Lacy reticular white striae and plaques on the dorsal tongue (panels A, D)
Reticular white keratosis on the lateral and ventral tongue (panels B, C)
Patchy depapillation and erythema between keratotic striae
Yellowish coating over the posterior dorsum in panel A
describe_en: Clinical photographs of the tongue in four patients with chronic graft-versus-host disease. The dorsal, lateral, and ventral surfaces show lacy reticular white striae and confluent white keratotic plaques set against patchy erythema and papillary atrophy. Panel A additionally shows a yellowish surface coating posteriorly, and panel D shows erythema of the lips. No exophytic mass or deep ulcer is seen. Findings are consistent with lichenoid oral cGVHD, a diagnostic manifestation by NIH consensus criteria.

ddx.vs: Morphologically near-identical lichenoid striae; distinction rests on transplant history and concurrent cGVHD in other organs rather than appearance.
Candida forms removable curd-like plaques or erythematous atrophy with fungal elements on smear, whereas lichenoid striae are fixed and reticular.
Hairy leukoplakia shows vertically corrugated white plaques confined to the lateral tongue and EBV positivity, not reticular lacy striae across the dorsum.
A homogeneous or verrucous fixed plaque without reticular pattern, or a persistent nonhealing area, warrants biopsy to exclude dysplasia, a recognized late risk in oral cGVHD.
